jobs.location: National Capital District, Morobe, Autonomous Region of Bougainville, Central, East Sepik, East New Britain, Eastern Highlands, Madang, Milne Bay, New Ireland, West New Britain, Western Highlands
jobs.employer_address: P. O Box 789, Port Moresby 121, Papua New Guinea
jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
Joining our geotechnical team, you will support safe and efficient mine operations by managing geotechnical hazards that could impact safety and business performance. Your expertise in slope design, stability analysis, and geotechnical data management will directly contribute to the success of short, medium, and long-term mine planning across the Lihir Operations.
As part of our team, you will
As a Supervisor (senior equivalent) Geotechnical Design Engineer, you will play a key role in shaping safe and efficient open-pit mining operations at Lihir. You will lead geotechnical investigations, deliver high-quality slope designs, and provide expert technical guidance that supports confident mine planning and risk management. This is an opportunity to influence major operational outcomes while developing and mentoring a high-performing technical team.
You will:
Provide technical expertise on pit slope design and slope management practices.
Collect, interpret, and analyse geotechnical data, including core logging, sampling, field testing, geological mapping, and UAV photogrammetry.
Conduct 2D and 3D slope stability modelling using software such as Rocscience suite (SLIDE2, SLIDE3D, RS2, RS3, DIPS, SWEDGE), FLAC 2D/3D (optional), GeoStudio, and other relevant tools.
Prepare detailed stability analysis reports and clearly communicate recommendations to support short, medium, and long-term mine planning.
Perform stability back-analysis for all fall-of-ground incidents and develop mitigation measures.
Support operational teams by integrating geotechnical monitoring data and contributing to risk management decisions.
Support mine operations in implementing and managing slope processes and systems, under the direction of the Geotechnical Superintendent.
Collaborate with consultants and stakeholders to collect data, refine models, and integrate monitoring information for long-term slope design and risk management.
Work with the Group Geotechnical team on slope designs with significant safety or operational implications, including LOPP and MTP projects.
Mentor and develop team members, graduates, and trainees in modelling, slope stability analysis, and geotechnical risk management.
Update and maintain geotechnical Ground Control Management Plan (GCMP).
Champion proactive safety behaviours and ensure full compliance with HSE standards.
Prerequisites for your success in this role
You bring strong technical expertise in geology or engineering, with hands-on experience in open-cut mine sites in both soft and hard rock. Safety, leadership, and adaptability are at the core of your approach. You take ownership of outcomes, embrace challenges, and deliver results under pressure while developing and guiding your team.
You will also bring:
Tertiary qualification in Bachelor of Science (Geology) or Engineering (Civil or Mining).
Currently holds, or is willing to obtain, accreditation from the Institute of Engineers Papua New Guinea (IEPNG).
Postgraduate qualifications in geotechnical engineering or project management are desirable.
Extensive geotechnical management experience in open-pit mining operations, including time spent in senior-level roles.
Strong proficiency in geotechnical modelling software (Rocscience suite, GeoStudio; FLAC desirable).
Experience with geotechnical database management (e.g., acQuire) and geological/mine planning software (Leapfrog, MineSight preferred).
Highly proficient in MS Office applications, including advanced use of Excel for data analysis and reporting.
Strong leadership, coaching, and interpersonal skills; able to mentor teams while embodying Newmont’s values and vision.
Open-minded, adaptable, and able to take on diverse challenges with effective prioritisation and time management.
Comprehensive knowledge of PNG Mine Safety Act and regulations.
Excellent analytical, planning, problem-solving, communication, and stakeholder engagement skills.
Your work environment
This role is based at Newmont’s Lihir Operations in Papua New Guinea and follows a 22:20 Fly-In, Fly-Out (FIFO) roster to Lihir Island. The position primarily operates on a day shift, with occasional night shift callouts as required.
You will work closely with the Geotechnical, Mine Operations, and Planning teams in a dynamic open pit environment. The role provides exposure to technically challenging geotechnical conditions and offers the opportunity to influence large-scale, complex mining projects.
Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp, in an en-suited and airconditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. A variety of healthy meal options are catered for at our mess; and the wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts.
Why Join Newmont
Be part of one of the world’s leading gold mining companies with a strong commitment to safety, sustainability, and community.
Work within a collaborative team of technical specialists and leaders who value innovation and continuous improvement.
Access opportunities for professional development, career mobility, and leadership growth.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you! 40645

About us
K92 Mining Limited operates the Kainantu Gold Mine in the Eastern Highlands Province. Since we launched in 2016, we've grown gold production every year, boosting Papua New Guinea's economy. We take pride in supporting your communities, with nearly 94% of our team members being fellow PNG locals.
Looking ahead, we will significantly increase our gold production in the next three years. This expansion means that K92 is a place for building a stable career, contributing to the community, and being a key part of our success.
About the role
The Plant Fitter is responsible to maintain all plant equipment and ensure all planning and scheduling maintenance activities are performed safely and more effectively. Also assist the Maintenance Foreman in performing preventative maintenance programs, perform routine maintenance and enforces statutory requirements and assist to create a zero-base safety culture.
Key / Major Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Reporting faults and Hazards and respond to routine emergency calls for repair and service within the plant site area.
Carrying our all-mechanical maintenance work safely and to the relevant standards.
Monitoring and assessment of plant and equipment to ensure optimal performance.
Completion of daily time sheet with the correct job numbers and time.
Assist in supervising and on-job training for Apprentices and Trade Assistance.
Willingness to assist other trades as and when required.
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential that you must have a NATTB certified Trade certificate in Fitting & Machining or Mechanical Fitting with 4+ years’ experience in mining environment. In addition to this, you will have some or all the following.
Sound knowledge of and familiar with all Gold Processing Plant Equipment.
Ability to trouble shoots and perform root cause analysis (particularly in diagnosis and fault finding).
Must be a self-starter and very resourceful.
Ability to find solutions to problems to ensure the equipment availability is maintained. Flexible, adaptable and be a team player.
Life at K92
Our core values — Collaboration, Accountability, Respect, Excellence, and Safety — are central to our operations and fundamental to our success. K92 upholds a commitment to equal opportunity, striving to ensure that every individual can reach their highest potential without experiencing discrimination.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
We believe in sharing our success with our employees. In addition to competitive salaries, we offer participation in long- and short-term incentive plans. We also offer savings programs, medical assistance, as well as access to our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
If you share our values and are looking for your next career step, come join us on this exciting journey. Submit your application through our website today.

About us
K92 Mining Limited operates the Kainantu Gold Mine in the Eastern Highlands Province. Since we launched in 2016, we've grown gold production every year, boosting Papua New Guinea's economy. We take pride in supporting your communities, with nearly 94% of our team members being fellow PNG locals.
Looking ahead, we will significantly increase our gold production in the next three years. This expansion means that K92 is a place for building a stable career, contributing to the community, and being a key part of our success.
About the role
The Permit to Work (PTW) Supervisor is a part of the Processing Department who leads and guides the permit to work team to ensure the energy control & isolations and permits to work are completed to a standard that ensures that safety, environmental, and operational risks are maintained at an impeccable standard for those relying upon them to safely complete their work.
Key / Major Accountabilities
Provide leadership, coaching and mentoring to a team of Permit Issuers in their role to ensure the PTW system is being followed, eliminating exposure to risks while workers are carrying out work.
Identify and carry out safe and effective isolations in the field to ensure the safety of all personnel who are required to perform work on the equipment.  Confirm IRS documents are correct and relevant to the job to be performed.  Create new IRS documents as required.
Verify that all necessary safety procedures and controls are in place before issuing any permit. This includes confirming of risk assessments, JSEAs, and required personal protective equipment (PPE).
Take part in shutdown planning meetings, prepare IRS documents in line with shutdown plan and work lists, ensuring they are prepared for issue in line with the shutdown schedule.
Perform isolations as per the shutdown schedule, prepare permit control boards and issue permits to those performing the work. Deisolate and return the plant to operating condition as jobs are completed on equipment items.
Work closely with supervisors and safety personnel to ensure that all isolation safety precautions are understood and implemented. Provide clear guidance to workers regarding the requirements outlined in the permit, emphasising safety and emergency procedures. Notify relevant stakeholders of any changes to work conditions or permits and ensure that any new permits or revised permits are issued promptly.
Before issuing a permit, review permit receiver’s JSEA and other related documents and ensure the documents are in line with the task. Ensure compliance with established isolation and permit practices, ensuring that all personnel involved in the work are adhering to safety regulations.
Maintain filing system where all completed and returned permits are scanned into the correct folders on the K92 Processing storage. Keep accurate and up-to-date records of all issued permits, including work details, personnel involved, safety precautions, and any changes made during the work process. Report any violations of safety protocols or non-compliance with issued permits to relevant supervisors or management. Ensure that records are complete and readily available for internal and external audits, ensuring compliance with safety regulations and standards.
Organise and document weekly safety toolbox meetings.
Carry out other relative duties as directed by the Coordinator Processing
Utilising available resources, maintain equipment to a safe and efficient standard in accordance with government regulations and company policy.
Cost control.
About You
To be considered for this role, you will have some or all the following.
High school diploma or equivalent. Technical diploma or higher in engineering, such as Processing, Mechanical or Electrical, or a related field is preferred
Certification in Occupational Health and Safety, First Aid, or a relevant PTW certification is highly recommended.
Familiarity with HSE Systems: Experience with Health, Safety, and Environmental management systems and regulations (e.g., OSHA, ISO 45001, etc.).
At least 3 years of PTW experience working in minerals Processing, Oil & Gas, construction, or maintenance environments, with a specific focus on safety management.
Have worked in the mineral processing or oil and gas industry in a similar role for at least 5 years.
Proactive and able to maintain continuous improvement of the PTW system.
Proven ability to lead a team of permit issuers
Ability to maintain the high-level standards required by a PTW team and infrastructure, equipment and tooling.
Exceptional planning and execution skills
Clear understanding of P&ID and PFD drawings
Demonstrated ability to lead a team in Energy control and isolation systems
Demonstrated ability to lead a team to maintain PTW activities including for high-risk tasks.
Demonstrated knowledge and understanding of Safety, environmental systems, procedures and standards
Demonstrated ability to work with planning and scheduling teams, for preparing isolations and permits for plant shutdowns
Experience with gas testing equipment control, care, servicing and testing.
Life at K92
Our core values — Collaboration, Accountability, Respect, Excellence, and Safety — are central to our operations and fundamental to our success. K92 upholds a commitment to equal opportunity, striving to ensure that every individual can reach their highest potential without experiencing discrimination.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
We believe in sharing our success with our employees. In addition to competitive salaries, we offer participation in long- and short-term incentive plans. We also offer savings programs, medical assistance, as well as access to our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
If you share our values and are looking for your next career step, come join us on this exciting journey. Submit your application through our website today.

POSITION TITLE:
Monitoring, Evaluation & Learning Coordinator
LOCATION:
KTF Port Moresby Office
TYPE / DURATION:
Full time, 12-month contract
REPORTING TO:
Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning Advisor
ABOUT KTF:
KTF is an Australian international aid and development organisation working in Papua New Guinea (PNG).
We work with people and communities to improve the lives and futures of Papua New Guineans. We do this by: assisting remote and rural communities with access to elementary and primary
education
;
improving access to quality and accessible
healthcare
;
improved
equality
and safety for women and girls; and by fostering the next generation of
leaders
.
KTF is a member of the Australian Council for International Development and is accredited with the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade’s Australian Not-for-Profit Cooperation Program.
Come and join the KTF family and enjoy working in a fast -paced, challenging environment with a great team in our Port Moresby office.
ABOUT THE ROLE:
The Monitoring, Evaluation & Learning (MEL) Coordinator plays a key role in our Port Moresby office supporting high-quality data collection, analysis and reporting across the organisation. This position works closely with the MEL Advisor and project teams to ensure monitoring systems are efficient, accurate and aligned with project outcomes and donor requirements
as we seek to impact lives and futures in remote and rural PNG.
RESPONSIBILITIES:
The role will be responsible for:
Work with the MEL Advisor to ensure timely and accurate reporting on all projects and in alignment with funding agreements and regulatory compliance;
Support the end-to-end M&E process across all projects, including coordination of planning, data collection, data management, analysis and reporting.
Assist in the design and administration of monitoring tools such as surveys and consultation guides, ensuring alignment with project indicators and donor requirements.
Coordinate logistics for data collection, including printing and packaging of monitoring tools, shipment to provinces, and providing technical support for in-field staff and partners.
Manage data quality processes including scanning, data entry and validation to ensure accuracy and completeness.
Conduct data analysis and contribute to interpretation of findings, including preparation of reports and data visualisations and key insights.
Contribute to quarterly reporting and the annual Effectiveness Results process by organising and presenting monitoring data.
Support in the management of KTF’s monitoring systems in Monday, Google Sheets, and Google Looker Studio (and others as developed/required)
Work with project teams to strengthen and streamline monitoring systems and promote consistent data collection practices across sites.
Assist in developing, maintaining and updating Monitoring & Evaluation Plans.
Support evaluation activities, including coordination of fieldwork logistics, preparation of data and evidence for evaluators.
Support impact reporting efforts, including managing, collating and filing case studies.
Provide training on MEL to partners and assist them with procedures to ensure efficiency of activities.
The role may be required to assist with some project support tasks.
The role may require assisting the Programs team with safeguarding, GEDSI and other cross-cutting issues.
YOUR SKILLS & ATTRIBUTES:
The ideal candidate will have:
A degree in a relevant field (social sciences, statistics, business, etc.)
A can-do attitude with fantastic problem-solving skills and thinks outside the box
Team player
Exceptional organisational skills
Advanced administrative skills – filing documents, scanning, printing, etc.
Ability to manage complex details across multiple projects
Ability to prioritise, think ahead, and use time management skills
Ability to work independently, as well as part of a team
Strong capability with the use of Microsoft Word/Google Docs, Excel/Google Sheets
Data Analysis skills – ability to analyse data sets in Excel/Sheets and understand data findings
Writing skills – ability to write engaging reports summarising findings, using quotes effectively
Familiarity with Dropbox and Google Drive
Ability to build a rapport with people and conduct interviews
Fluency in English & Tok Pisin – and the ability to translate documents
Ability to travel to remote and rural areas of Papua New Guinea.
Desired:
Some work experience (casual, part-time, or full-time)
Familiarity with survey platforms such as Google Forms, Kobotoolbox, Jotform, etc.
Interest or experience in community development or working in the NGO sector
Demonstrated research experience
Understanding of M&E principles
Willingness to work with remote teams in other locations in PNG and Australia

About us

More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
In this role you will Coordinate all HSE activities under the direction from the Superintendent - HSE and Manager- HSE with a strong focus on underground operations and coach the graduate safety officers. As Safety Coordinator you will provide advice and guidance to site Departments and contractors on safety related matters, implementation of the K92 Safety programs and managing the site safety database.
Key Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Maintain a safe work environment for all K92 employees, visitors and contractors through audits, inspections, and training.
Support Department and Contractor Safety Officer’s and Safety Representatives as required in the successful performance of their duties.
Ensure all incidents are fully investigated and recorded within the site safety data base in a timely and accurate manner.
Specific focus to underground operations
Participate in workplace inspections and audits.
Manage the safety team in terms of work location, tasks, priorities – in consultation with the OHSET Superintendent.
Act as a role model for all Safety Officers.
Conduct scheduled weekly and monthly safety audits and checks site wide.
Ensuring that the camp and mine site safety regulations are observed by all K92 employees and contractors.
Provide safety induction to new intakes, casuals, contractors, and visitors to site
About You
To be considered for this position, candidates must have 10 years minimum Safety work experience in an extractive industry or heavy construction environment. In addition to this, candidates should also (ideally) be able to demonstrate some or all the following.
Appropriate Safety Officer qualifications (Cert IV OHS minimum).
Significant experience with auditing, incident reporting.
Incident investigation training (preferably ICAM
Well versed with safety systems that deals with compliance records and reports.
Excellent oral and written communications skills.
Very good end user of MS Office Suite: Word, Excel and Outlook.

Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.

About Us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners of the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea — more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG — and our local education and skills development initiatives, which include educational scholarships, agricultural support, and health outreach programs, help to improve quality of life and build long-term capacity in local communities.
About the Role
The Principal – Business Development is responsible for driving sustainable local business participation across K92’s supply chain. This role links operational procurement needs with community enterprise capabilities, fostering opportunities across the mine life cycle, from exploration support services to closure-related remediation contracts.
The role supervises the Superintendent – Business Development, who implements supplier readiness programs, delivers business training, and coordinates enterprise development activities.
Key Accountabilities
This position provides strategic direction and operational oversight for landowner and local enterprise development. Part of the responsibilities include:
Lead and Manage Business Development:
Direct and mentor the Superintendent – Business Development, set clear annual objectives and budgets, and collaborate with Supply Chain to identify procurement opportunities for local SMEs.
Strategic Partnerships & Capacity Building:
Develop partnerships with training institutions, NGOs, and financial service providers to strengthen supplier capacity and promote long-term business sustainability.
Governance & Compliance:
Embed SPMS Technical Standards into all business development initiatives, ensuring compliance, audit-readiness, and alignment with corporate governance frameworks.
Local Business Participation:
Increase the number and value of contracts awarded to local suppliers, contributing to economic growth and ensuring compliance with MOA local content commitments.
Annual Planning & Reporting:
Prepare annual business development plans and budgets; report quarterly on procurement outcomes, supplier performance, and training impacts.
Delegation & Financial Authority:
Approve expenditure within allocated budgets and authorise the engagement of external service providers for training and capacity-building programs.
About You
To be considered for this position, candidates must have substantial experience working with resource project landowners and business development in Papua New Guinea. In addition to this, candidates should also be able to demonstrate and have some or all of the following:
• Bachelor’s degree in Business, Economics, or Supply Chain Management.
• Substantial experience in procurement, supplier development, or enterprise growth in resource-sector contexts.
• Proven cross-cultural engagement skills and ability to manage community expectations around procurement.
• Strong commercial acumen and understanding of PNG’s SME landscape.
• Sound knowledge of business development frameworks and legislation, including the PNG Companies Act (1997).
• PNG Driver’s License Class 6 is essential.
• Strong financial and business management skills, with experience in budgeting, cost control, and operational improvement.
• High-level communication skills in English and Tok Pisin, with the ability to engage rural and village-based communities.

Our core values —
Collaboration, Accountability, Respect, Excellence, and Safety
— are central to our operations and fundamental to our success. K92 upholds a commitment to equal opportunity, striving to ensure that every individual can reach their highest potential without experiencing discrimination.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable TV, and a gymnasium.

We also offer savings programs, medical assistance, and access to our wellbeing and employee assistance programs, all supported by a friendly roster system.

Join PNG Motors and work across PNG’s strongest automotive brands.

PNG Motors is strengthening its technical team, and the Auto Electrician role sits at the centre of our workshop performance. We’re looking for a qualified, confident, and skilled sparky who understands the complexity of modern vehicle electronics — someone who takes pride in delivering work that is clean, precise, and reliable.
In this role, you’ll handle diagnostics, repairs, and installations across a wide range of brands, including Hyundai, Mazda, Ford, Suzuki, JMC and Joylong. High performers who don’t cut corners.

jobs.description:
ORGANISATION:
Kokoda Track Foundation (KTF)
POSITION: Secondary FODE Teacher
LOCATION:
Various
DURATION:
Academic year with 6-month probationary period
REMUNERATION:
Competitive remuneration offered
ABOUT KTF FODE COLLEGES:
The KTF FODE Colleges are training facilities located in mostly rural locations throughout Papua New Guinea. The FODE Centers deliver curriculum to students to upgrade their certifications making them eligible to follow teaching and health worker professional studies pathways.
The FODE Centres are currently running the Flexible Open Distance Education (FODE) program, upskilling members of the community through the FODE curriculum of assessments and examinations all the way through to their Grade 12 certificates.
We are currently recruiting high-achieving, independent and self-motivated, skilled professionals with the required registration for our colleges. Someone that is dedicated, innovative, flexible and team orientated. You will work with a small team to support the growth of our colleges and the success of the students following the FODE curriculum, this remote management will necessitate excellent communication skills.
The role is hands-on and will require the successful candidate to undertake a variety of tasks, including teaching, assessment, written and verbal feedback of student work, mentoring, administration of enrolments, developing strategies in maintaining student progress, supporting the community engagement with the facility, maintaining a student database, and maintaining regular contact with KTF.
ABOUT THE ROLE:
Key Responsibilities:
Conduct the teaching, marking, assessment and monitoring of FODE Curriculum and determine instructional and assessment strategies to suit a range of student needs;
Oversee and set student targets in accordance with the requirements of the curriculum;
Establish and maintain a positive learning environment, including encouraging students to take responsibility for their own learning;
Motivate and monitor students through the cycle of remote and on-site learning;
Support students as they approach and take exams to be fully prepared and confident with the process and material;
Research, prepare and customise learning materials suitable for a range of teaching and learning settings and a range of students;
Maintain accurate records of students’ attendance, progress and assessment and communicate these to the FODE Centre Principals and Project Management in Australia;
A good understanding and competence of technology for email communications, database entry and marketing as well as being able to manage an electronic version of FODE materials via tablet technology;
Open to learning how to use tablet technology to deliver the FODE program;
Any other duties as directed by the College Management;
Adhere to all KTF policies and procedures including child protection policy, no-alcohol, drugs & buai policy, disability policy, gender equity policy, and counter terrorism
LOCATIONS
KTF is currently recruiting Secondary Teachers / FODE Lecturers for the following locations. Please indicate in your application what location preferences you have.
Kokoda College, Oro Province
Kiunga, Western Province
Morehead, Western Province
Lake Murray, Western Province
New Ireland Province (Lihir Island and Namatanai District)
KEY SELECTION CRITERIA
Applicants must demonstrate they are able to meet the following Key Selection Criteria:
Bachelor degree of Education – Secondary Education
ESSENTIAL
;
Full teaching registration obtained
ESSENTIAL
;
Minimum 5 years teaching experience (secondary teaching)
HIGHLY DESIRED
;
Possess current vocational skills and knowledge that will enable vocational training and education programs in the relevant teaching areas to be prepared, delivered, assessed, evaluated and administered;
Possess the ability to research, select and use a wide range of teaching and assessment strategies to suit the needs of a diverse range of students, including those with disabilities and from other disadvantaged groups;
Possess the ability to apply information and communication technologies to the teaching and learning process as well as collecting, organising and processing relevant data;
High level of communication, mentoring and interpersonal skills, and the ability to work independently or as a member of a team;
Knowledge and understanding of the current issues influencing the TVET sector, particularly with teacher education colleges;
Experience with the FODE program is desirable
OTHER REQUIREMENTS:
Applicants must have the right to work in PNG.
This position may require travel within PNG from time to time.
KTF is a child safe organisation committed to the protection of people we serve. Our recruitment and selection procedures are designed to ensure we only recruit people who are suitable and aligned with our policies that ensure the safety of children and the protection of all from sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment. All appointments are subject to appropriate background checks and screening and the successful candidate will be required to get a Working With Children check and/or a Police Clearance Certificate. We promote diversity and equality in all our practices and strongly encourage those with diverse backgrounds and/or disabilities and or those who identify as LGBTQI+ to apply.

A cover letter addressing the following:

Secondary FODE Teacher;

Your current resume;

ESSENTIAL
;
Attach at least one written reference
ESSENTIAL

jobs.title: Tebbutt Research PNG
jobs.description:
Tebbutt Research PNG - Graduate Field Coordinator
Are you a young professional looking for an exciting and challenging career in the market and social research industry with a regional market leader and internationally recognised firm?
Do you have a degree qualification from a recognised university?
Do you have up to 2 years of commercial work experience?
Are you a motivated team player?
If this sounds like you, then you might be the person we are looking for!
The Company
Tebbutt Research is an ISO-20252-certified business that specialises in market and social research. We have been established for over 30 years and our clients include prominent multinational corporations, respected donor organizations and governments. We are the industry leader in the Pacific Islands, where we work across 22 countries. We have won numerous awards over the years and have a great, close-knit team and a supportive work culture.
Research fields include customer satisfaction, ad and communications testing, brand development, media ratings, segmentation studies, product testing, and monitoring and evaluation surveys. The techniques used include qualitative research, quantitative research, data analysis, observation, and audit methods.
The Role
We now have an opportunity for a professional to join our small executive team in Port Moresby as Graduate Field Coordinator. This role covers a range of project and people tasks both in the office and in the field, including:
coordination of our fieldwork teams of interviewers, including running project briefings, conducting field visits, monitoring team progress, and planning logistics
providing accurate and timely reporting on fieldwork status to the field management team
following our fieldwork compliance requirements for ISO using our existing procedures
regular travel domestically in PNG to conduct small team briefings and check on team progress
checking questionnaire scripts that are programmed onto tablet devices by our data team to see that they work correctly before running briefings with the fieldwork team
supporting the PNG General Manager as required
The role suits a person with flexibility in working hours, including work into early evenings and on weekends as necessary.
You will report to the PNG General Manager with line reporting to the Regional Operations Manager.
The Person
You must have a university degree in any field including business, with a good academic record.
You will ideally have up to 2 years of commercial work experience in any field, but newer graduates are also welcome to apply. An understanding of any of the following fields would be an advantage but not essential: market research, operations, information technology, project management, or human resources.
The role will suit you if you are interested in human behaviour, in learning to lead small teams of people, and logistics. You will have the following qualities:
a genuine interest in people’s views and opinions
the confidence to learn to lead teams
good communication skills and the ability to communicate with people from all walks of life
the highest level of personal integrity and honesty
a team player attitude and like working collaboratively
a quality focus
a high standard of written and spoken English
Details
Salary and benefits are commensurate with skills and experience.
If this sounds like you, we would like to hear from you! Please forward a copy of your CV and cover letter for consideration. Please email your application to
[email protected]
and all applications will be treated in strict confidence.
Apply

jobs.title: Logistics Supervisor
jobs.description:
Logistics Supervisor
Position Summary
The Logistics Supervisor
is responsible for coordinating the services in P.N.G to support the flow of materials for client projects on an end-to-end basis.
Position Responsibilities
The Logistics Supervisor is responsible and accountable for overseeing and coordinating all logistics operations to ensure the efficient and compliant movement of goods to and from project sites. This includes managing team performance, ensuring adherence to company procedures, and maintaining strong relationships with key stakeholders.
Key responsibilities include (but are not limited to):
Supervise and coordinate the logistics team to ensure the efficient flow of goods from various origins to project sites, in line with delivery SOPs, including freight booking, document control, packing, storage, and quarantine compliance.
Oversee and confirm the arrival of goods at ports of import/export within PNG, ensuring clearance procedures are managed effectively in coordination with customs agents and service providers.
Monitor and review customs processes to ensure timely release of cargo, taking proactive measures to prevent delays, port storage, or detention costs.
Identify and implement improvements to streamline logistics operations and reduce cycle times between cargo arrival, customs clearance, and final delivery.
Maintain oversight of the release and movement of goods from wharf to site or warehouse, ensuring timely, accurate, and transparent status updates.
Supervise inspection activities, including visual checks and line-item verification to confirm cargo accuracy against packing lists and documentation.
Ensure compliance with domestic and international transport requirements, coordinating repacking, fumigation, or certification activities with relevant service providers as needed.
Coordinate and oversee import and export clearances, working closely with freight forwarders, customs brokers, and internal stakeholders to ensure documentation accuracy and timeliness.
Maintain and review shipment tracking reports, ensuring accurate and up-to-date visibility of cargo movement and performance metrics.
Ensure data integrity through accurate and timely entry of logistics information into internal systems, and review entries completed by the logistics team.
Oversee job file management, verifying the completeness and accuracy of records for invoicing, accruals, and third-party billing.
Support and guide the Logistics team, providing leadership, mentoring, and performance feedback to ensure consistent delivery of high-quality service.
Maintain professional communication with internal teams, clients, and service providers, proactively addressing and resolving operational or compliance issues.
Report to the Logistics Lead, providing regular operational updates, data insights, and recommendations for process improvement.
Selection Criteria – Essential
Strong planning, organizing, and attention to detail.
Proficient in Microsoft Office.
Strong communication (verbal and written) and interpersonal skills.
Ability to work independently and within a team.
Selection Criteria – Desirable
+5 years operational experience in freight forwarding and customs clearance.
Familiarity with  logistics systems.
Experience working with shipping or freight forwarding companies.
Financial understanding of logistics cost drivers and structure.
Qualifications / Licences
Minimum Year 12 Accreditation
Current unrestricted drivers licence – Manual preferred

About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. Joining our underground mining team, this role reports to the Shotcrete Supervisor and is required to ensure that all aspects of shotcrete spraying are carried out in a safe and efficient manner and in accordance with K92 Mining site requirements and procedures

Operate a shotcrete rig and underground equipment to apply fibrecrete

Conduct QA/QC tests, maintain equipment, and support daily mining operations.
Work closely with the Mining shift boss to assess performance and identify improvements to maximise results, reduce risk and minimise wastage of consumables.
Responsible for ongoing communication with supervisors.

Responsible for housekeeping as per standard.
Maintain work relationship with all working crews during shift hours.
Responsible to safely operate the equipment.
Actively promotes a safe and healthy culture.

Experience in shotcrete spraying

Maintain clear communication regarding orders status and delivery schedules.

Assign tasks and coordinate workflow to meet production deadlines.
Train staff on equipment operation, safety protocols and quality standards.
Conduct performance evaluations and provide constructive feedback.
Organize and lead team meetings to discuss production goals and challenges.
Foster a collaborative and productive work environment.

Expertise in heat press operations for various materials.
Knowledge of sublimation printing processes and applications.
Experience with restringing for sports equipment and rackets.
Understanding of materials, substrates and production methods.

Strong leadership and team management capabilities.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
Proven customer service orientation and problem-solving ability.
Experience managing high-volume and bulk order work flows.
Attention to detail and commitment to quality standards.
Ability to multitask and prioritize in fast-paced environment.

jobs.title: SGSC Geomechanic
jobs.employer_address:
PO Box 842
Port Moresby
NCD 121
Papua New Guinea
jobs.description:
Don’t come for an easy career. Stay for a rewarding one.
Santos is a global energy company committed to increasingly cleaner energy and fuels production, with operations across Australia, Papua New Guinea, Timor-Leste and North America.
We are currently PNG’s largest single investor and most active explorer, operating all the country’s producing oil fields and holding an extensive appraisal and exploration portfolio. Our aspirations and strategies reflect our genuine commitment to making a meaningful contribution to the lives of Papua New Guineans.
At Santos, our commitment is to be a global leader in the transition to cleaner energy and clean fuels, by helping the world decarbonise to reach net-zero emissions in an affordable and sustainable way.
Santos is one of Australia’s biggest domestic gas supplier, a leading Asia Pacific LNG supplier and is committed to supplying the critical fuels such as oil and gas in a more sustainable way through decarbonising projects such as the Moomba CCS project.
For more than 65 years, Santos has been working in partnership with local communities, providing local jobs and business opportunities, safely and sustainably developing its natural gas resources, and powering industries and households.
What you’ll do:
The Geomechanic will play a key role in establishing Santos’ PNG National Lead Support Centre in Port Moresby.
You’ll work closely with the Geomechanics Group to provide expert support across a range of studies, including wellbore stability, pore pressure and fracture gradient prediction, subsidence and fracture modelling, seal integrity, sand/fines production, natural fracture characterisation, and fault and cap seal analysis.
Given the scope of the SGSC’s work, the role involves collaboration with teams across Santos’ assets and may require travel to field locations as necessary.
Key Responsibilities
Complete offset well reviews with a focus on geomechanical issues, including wellbore stability, losses, and fracture stimulation challenges.
Contribute to pre-drill and while-drilling assessments of in situ stress, pore pressure, and fracture gradient.
Provide geomechanics support to multidisciplinary studies across all business areas, including conventional and unconventional reservoirs and Carbon Sequestration projects.
Integrate core and image log-scale fracture and fault interpretations with broader seismic interpretation, including analysis of image logs and core.
Supervise rock strength testing of core samples.
Apply Santos standard file management, archiving processes, and procedures to project files for Technical Assistants.
Foster a technical environment that promotes cross-discipline collaboration, generation of new ideas, and technical excellence.
Represent the SGSC, upholding Santos’ values and behavioural expectations with internal and external stakeholders.
Ensure compliance with the Santos Management System (SMS), Delegation of Authority (DOA), and Corporate Governance and Safety requirements.
What you’ll bring:
Essential experience:
Demonstrate some experience in geoscience or engineering roles.
Hold a tertiary qualification in geoscience or a relevant engineering discipline.
Apply a high level of computer literacy in MS Excel, Word, PowerPoint, and Access.
Communicate effectively, both orally and in writing, to liaise with internal Santos stakeholders.
Build and maintain strong working relationships within a culturally diverse workforce.
Work independently with limited direction, meet deadlines, and perform effectively under pressure.
Desirable experience:
Apply knowledge or experience of drilling and subsurface operations.
Utilise a broad range of industry software, such as Wellview, RokDoc, Petrel, or equivalent.
Technical Competencies
Analyse reservoir geomechanics, including in-situ stress, pore pressure, and natural fracturing.
Plan and assess wellbore stability, including mud window calculations and failure mitigation.
Understand and recognise the mechanisms for over and under-pressure and compute basic PPFG plots
Apply laboratory testing to derive rock strength and deformability parameters.
Analyse seal integrity analysis using Fault plane orientation relative to regional stress field (fault seal prediction) and/or top seal integrity using capillary pressure and brittleness/strength indicators
Interpret hydraulic fracture data (Frac, DFIT, XLOT, LOT, FIT) and derive rock mechanics properties.
Analyse pressure data to prepare potentiometric surfaces, water classification, and salinity maps
What you’ll get:
Here, you’ll be amongst high-calibre people and get to work on industry-leading projects. We don’t shy away from solving tough problems at pace. We like it that way. You can expect to be challenged and supported; to learn and grow.
At Santos, we’re committed to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive. This means a place that is safe; where you are valued and respected, and your contribution is recognised and appreciated. Join us, and you’ll play a role in this too.
Each of our sites offer access to specific amenities that aim to create the best possible benefits to your health, wellbeing and performance.
What you’re part of:
Everywhere you turn you will be a part of a team who are coming together to contribute to our single uniting purpose - to provide reliable and affordable energy to help create a better world for everyone
And because it’s not only what you do, but how you do it, you will also contribute to improving the living standards of the communities where we operate, building enduring and respectful relationships that serve a generation. It’s about each of us, and all of us – together.
How to Apply
Applications must be submitted via the online recruitment system before
COB Friday 28th November 2025.
A requirement of this role is that you will need to have in place the legal work rights for PNG to apply.
Potential Scams
There are a number of fake adverts that are impersonating Santos Limited, in these instances you will receive an e-mail from a generic e-mail address. We do not make offers without interviews or due diligence taking place. You will know if an advert is genuine if you are directed to the Santos company careers page to apply which is
https://recruitment.santos.com/

Don’t come for an easy career. Stay for a rewarding one.
Santos is a global energy company committed to increasingly cleaner energy and fuels production, with operations across Australia, Papua New Guinea, Timor-Leste and North America.
We are currently PNG’s largest single investor and most active explorer, operating all the country’s producing oil fields and holding an extensive appraisal and exploration portfolio. Our aspirations and strategies reflect our genuine commitment to making a meaningful contribution to the lives of Papua New Guineans.
At Santos, our commitment is to be a global leader in the transition to cleaner energy and clean fuels, by helping the world decarbonise to reach net-zero emissions in an affordable and sustainable way.
Santos is one of Australia’s biggest domestic gas supplier, a leading Asia Pacific LNG supplier and is committed to supplying the critical fuels such as oil and gas in a more sustainable way through decarbonising projects such as the Moomba CCS project.

Through strong leadership and financial stewardship, this position drives informed decision-making and ensures alignment with organisational priorities.

Financial Reporting Leadership: Coordinate and lead the financial reporting cycles, including monthly, quarterly, and annual reporting, ensuring timely and accurate consolidation of PNG asset results and commentary.

Quality Assurance: Review outputs from Finance Business Partners to ensure accuracy, completeness, and quality of financial analysis and reporting.
Data Integrity and Allocations Expertise: Serve as the subject matter expert for data and allocations, managing controls and logic to ensure accurate cost recovery from Joint Venture partners.
Process Improvement: Drive initiatives to enhance the quality and timeliness of financial data and analytics across the organisation.
Tool Development and Optimisation: Lead the development and enhancement of reporting tools, such as Power BI, to support budgeting, forecasting, and reporting requirements effectively.
What you'll bring:
Professional Experience

A minimum of 10 years appropriately related work experience.

Experience in recommending and implementing process improvements relating to systems and reporting.

Senior Surveyor.
About the role
Reporting to the Superintendent- Construction Projects, the Senior Surveyor is responsible for leading and managing all surveying activities associated with large-scale capital infrastructure projects. This role involves planning, executing, and overseeing land, construction, and engineering surveys to ensure accurate data collection, alignment, and compliance with project specifications and regulatory standards. The Senior Surveyor collaborates closely with project engineers, planners, and construction teams to support successful project delivery from inception to completion.
In this role, you will.
Lead and coordinate surveying activities for capital projects including topographical surveys, boundary surveys, construction staking, and as-built surveys.
Interpret and analyze project plans, drawings, and specifications to develop accurate survey methodologies and work plans.
Conduct site inspections to assess conditions and resolve surveying challenges in the field.
Manage survey data collection, processing, and quality assurance to ensure high accuracy and reliability.
Prepare detailed survey reports, maps, and documentation for use by engineering and construction teams.
Supervise and mentor junior surveyors and field technicians, ensuring adherence to safety and quality standards.
Coordinate with project stakeholders, including contractors, engineers, architects, and regulatory agencies.
Ensure all surveying activities comply with relevant legal, environmental, and safety regulations.
Utilize advanced surveying equipment such as total stations, GPS/GNSS, drones, and laser scanning technology.
Assist in budget planning and resource allocation for surveying components of capital projects.
Troubleshoot and resolve technical issues related to surveying and measurement.
Work with other seniors, surveyors and contractors to complete projects works on sites outside of the SML
Maintain a high level of health, safety and environmental awareness and comply with all relevant NPL policies & procedures.
About You

jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
As a Lead People Business Partner, reporting to the Director People, you will play a critical role in shaping workforce strategies, ensuring compliance with labour agreements, and fostering a positive employee experience. Your leadership will directly influence operational success and organizational culture at our Lihir site.
As Part of Our Team, You Will
Provide leadership, coaching and supervision to the People Business Partner team on day to day operational matters
Lead workforce planning and analysis.
Provide advisory support to leaders on all People-related matters.
Execute non-escalated investigations and disciplinary matters in line with standards and procedures.
Manage labour unrest risks and ensure compliance with CBAs.
Support and deliver enterprise led programs and initiatives within the operations by collaborating with other functions within the People Team.
Oversee workplace resources and administrative services.
Foster an inclusive team environment that encourages collaboration and feedback.
Prerequisites for Your Success in This Role
Education:
Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, or related field.
Experience:
Advanced knowledge in labour relations, disciplinary processes, and project execution.
Skills:
Strong leadership, supervisory of teams and interpersonal skills.
Expertise in workforce planning, HR system and processes, employee relations, and risk management.
Advanced coaching and change management capabilities.
Foundational knowledge of workplace resource administration.
Ability to influence, negotiate, and resolve conflicts effectively.
Ability to collaborate and work collaboratively at all levels of the organisation.
Your Work Environment
This is a residential opportunity offering secure and comfortable family accommodation in a gated community. You’ll enjoy a balanced 5:2 roster that allows you to return home to your family every evening, along with the benefits of tropical island living. Our residential village includes a range of social and recreational facilities such as an on-site gym, basketball court, and a café and deli offering takeaway coffees, snacks, and local and imported groceries, including fresh fruit. Based at Newmont’s Lihir site in PNG, you’ll work closely with site leaders and a team of six Business Partners and three Officers in a dynamic, collaborative environment where adaptability is key.
Why Join Newmont
At Newmont, we value safety, inclusion, and innovation. Joining us means being part of a global leader in mining, where your contributions drive meaningful change and sustainable growth. We offer competitive benefits, career development opportunities, and a culture that prioritizes your well-being.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply before the closing date: 25 November 2025 – we’d love to hear from you!

jobs.title: Cost Controller/Business Analyst
jobs.description:
Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited operates the Kainantu Gold Mine in the Eastern Highlands Province. Since we launched in 2016, we've grown gold production every year, boosting Papua New Guinea's economy. We take pride in supporting your communities, with nearly 94% of our team members being fellow PNG locals.
Looking ahead, we will significantly increase our gold production in the next three years. This expansion means that K92 is a place for building a stable career, contributing to the community, and being a key part of our success.
About the role
This role is responsible to provide to provide department managers & superintendents with necessary information to be able to control their costs/budgets, month-end financial transaction reviews and to continually improve the business systems and processes within the Department to enhance efficiency, budget compliance and overall cost effectiveness.
Key / Major Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Track daily expenditure and provide daily, weekly, and monthly cost variance analysis reports to all Sections within the Asset Management Department.
Assist in preparing the Department’s end-of-month and quarterly cost reports. This includes detailed commentary explaining both positive and negative variances to budget.
Review invoicing from Contractors and ensure that POs are approved, receipted, and are accurate and paid in a timely manner.
Assist in the preparation of annual (3 year) operating budgets.
Assist in preparation of CERs.
Assist in sourcing quotations and creating Purchase Requisitions for goods and services.
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential that you must a bachelor’s degree and/or Graduate Diploma in Business/Business Administration with CPA, CA, CMA or equivalent accounting designation is desirable. You must have a minimum of 5 years experience in a Cost Controller or Business Analyst role – preferably in the mining industry. In addition to this, you will have some or all the following.
Good level of English literacy - sound report writing skills, with use of finance and accounting terminology.
Good level of competency using the MS Office suite (MS Word, MS Excel and MS Power Point).
Familiarity/experience with Pronto ERP – specifically Finance, Supply and Maintenance modules.
Project Management experience – coordinating small projects.
Life at K92
Our core values — Collaboration, Accountability, Respect, Excellence, and Safety — are central to our operations and fundamental to our success. K92 upholds a commitment to equal opportunity, striving to ensure that every individual can reach their highest potential without experiencing discrimination.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
We believe in sharing our success with our employees. In addition to competitive salaries, we offer participation in long- and short-term incentive plans. We also offer savings programs, medical assistance, as well as access to our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
If you share our values and are looking for your next career step, come join us on this exciting journey. Submit your application through our website today.

jobs.description:
Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
Joining our Commercial team, you will undertake all regular purchasing and administrative duties including updating of purchasing records and pricing system. Another demand defined to this role is regular liaison with both local and overseas Suppliers and Service Providers with the prime objective of quality and on-time delivery of goods and services to meet site operational requirements. Moreover, this role involves preparation and processing of purchase orders and relating documents in line with K92 Mining Limited Supply and Procurement guidelines.
Key Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position mean you will
Ensure all supplies especially critical items required by end users are sourced and purchased and available for use without delay.
Carry out and monitor all purchasing duties.
Monitor stock levels based on the usage track record so that essential plant, mobile and light vehicle parts are available
Prepare and process purchase orders and supporting documents.
Purchase and issue order in accordance to specification.
Regular liaison with Warehouse and Logistics team to ensure orders are picked up in the shortest possible time.
Source, select and negotiate for the best quote price, terms and deliveries with suppliers/service providers.
Monitor and coordinate delivery of items between suppliers both local and overseas.
Constant liaison with suppliers on supplies and back orders and for logistical arrangements to site in a safe and timely manner.
Update and maintain purchasing records/data.
Maintain regular professional approach with various suppliers and service providers.
Maintain safe work standards and practices in accordance company policy.
Perform all roles and responsibilities that support and reflect the company’s mission and core values
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential that you have the following
A certificate or Diploma in business studies, Accounting or related field preferred but not essential
Five year’s work experience in a warehouse or purchasing role is well regarded
Must be a self-starter, very resourceful and with ability to find solutions.
Good oral and written communication skills.
Flexible, adaptable and be a team player
Ability to meet communicated schedules and deadlines.
Strong planning and organizational skills.
Proficient in computer use especially Microsoft suite, especially Excel and Outlook.
Proficient user of Pronto Xi Software is essential.
Mining Industry experience preferred.
Life at K92
K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.
In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.

About the Role:
We are seeking an experienced General Manager to lead a stable, diversified business in Lae, PNG. This is a high-profile role overseeing multiple divisions within a diversified business spanning agriculture, wholesales and commercial ventures. The successful candidate will drive growth, capture new opportunities, and position the business for long-term value creation.

Drive business growth, including commercialising assets, exploring export opportunities.
Lead multiple divisions including agriculture, animal production, property and feed operations.
Manage sales, commercial operations, and strategic initiatives across all divisions.
Oversee a workforce of ~600 employees within a broader group of ~1,300, building capability and fostering a high-performance culture.
Support shareholder objectives, including strategic investments/divestments, partnerships and alignment with business priorities.
Provide strong operational leadership, including change management, process improvement, and risk management.
Engage with Boards, partners, regulators, investors and community stakeholders.

Energetic, growth-oriented, and results-driven leader with demonstrated commercial acumen and a track record of delivering strong performance across multiple business units or divisions.
Proven experience in organisational change, transformation, and operational improvements.

Experience in import/export, sales, and commercial operations.
Strong leadership skills with the ability to manage diverse teams and large, multi-division operations.
Strategic and hands-on leader able to identify and capitalise on new business opportunities and ensure their successful implementation.
Skilled in engaging Boards, investors, and key stakeholders while ensuring strong governance, financial oversight, and delivery of strategic objectives.

Lead a high-profile, multi-division business with significant growth and commercial potential.
Opportunity to shape the strategic direction, operational performance, and long-term value creation of a diversified organisation.
Work closely with senior leadership and Boards, influencing major business decisions and strategic initiatives.
Manage a substantial workforce, building capability and fostering a high-performance culture.

PLEASE NOTE THAT THIS POSITION IS FOR A PRINCIPAL TO BE BASED IN BALIMO COLLEGE CAMPUS IN WESTERN PROVINCE, PNG. BEFORE APPLYING, PLEASE ENSURE THAT YOU HAVE THE RELEVANT NURSING AND ACADEMIC QUALIFICATIONS, EXPERIENCE, AND THE ABILITY TO RELOCATE TO WESTERN PROVINCE
ORGANISATION:

POSITION:

LOCATION:

COMMENCEMENT:

DURATION:
12-month contract with a 3-month probationary period
REMUNERATION:
Competitive remuneration package offered
REPORTING TO:
Chair, Balimo College Governing Council
ABOUT BALIMO COLLEGE:
Balimo College is Western Province’s newest Higher Education Institute. In 2025, Balimo College opened the new School of Nursing and commenced a 4-year Bachelor of General Nursing program. The College’s vision is to advance Western Province by providing high-quality education, research and community engagement. The institute will foster pathways for teachers and nurses who are committed to improving access to vital services in Western Province.
Balimo College is a safe and supportive place for graduates and other professionals across the Western Province catchment region to return for life-long learning and ongoing professional development. The College will develop a community of education and health professionals committed to innovation, excellence and community advancement; by being the training College of choice for Papua New Guineans.
Balimo College is a PNG Sustainable Development Program (SDP) initiative delivered in partnership with KTF, Divine Word University, and Western Sydney University. Balimo College School of Nursing is an affiliate of Divine Word University.

The Balimo College School of Nursing Principal is responsible for upholding the College’s Vision, Mission, Core Values, Educational Philosophy and Goals. The Principal will operate within the Balimo College School of Nursing leadership structure as determined by the Chair, Governing Council, to disseminate strong, effective educational leadership, and manage all information technology within the parameters identified in this position description.
The Principal will have an in-depth knowledge of the ethos and purpose of the Balimo College School of Nursing and the principles by which it operates. The Principal will have a firm understanding of the Western Province health context and the objectives of Balimo College School of Nursing to create pathways for rural communities into the field of nursing.

Simberi Gold Company Limited forms part of the St Barbara Group. Our Simberi Operations consists of an open cut mine on the northernmost island in the Tabar group of islands in the province of New Ireland in Papua New Guinea. Our vision is to grow sustainably and create enduring, positive impacts for the people and communities touched by our operations.
Now is an exciting time for our business and for our people. We’re going through a period of significant change and are gaining momentum in transforming our business. We’re looking for people who are ready to grow through opportunity and build a bright future with us.
We are currently seeking a
Graduate
Mine Engineer
to join our team. permanent full-time position at our Simberi Operation. Your work location is Papua New Guinea, working a 15/13 Roster from Kavieng, Rabaul, Port Moresby, Lae, Mt Hagen, Buka, Madang, Goroka, Alotau, Wapenamanda, Popondetta, Hoskins, Wewak, Vanimo or Tabar group of Islands.
(Locals are encouraged to apply)
.
Reporting to the MTS Superintendent, the Graduate Mine Engineer, is responsible to assist in the preparation of the short term (< 3 Mths) mine engineering and mine planning activities, ensuring Simberi Operations adheres to the site business plans and strategy to realise maximum return for the asset. The role will also provide technical and processional leadership and support to the Simberi Operations, which will be consistent with the Company’s Vision, Values and Policies.
The opportunity
Work with the technical services and mining teams to develop short term schedules in line with company targets and objectives.
Participate in the SGCL graduate program.
Support the mining operations team to achieve production targets by providing technical support in terms of mine design and planning.
Assist the mining engineer in the development and implementation of mine planning and scheduling system, processes, and procedures.
Assist the mining engineer with their efforts to ensure that the mine planning team provides a consistently high level of support to mining operations at Simberi.
Coordinate and consult with the mining department and the tech services team to ensure that all the daily mining and planning activities are conducted in a manner which allows safe and efficient mining operations.
Assist with tracking, reporting and analysis of daily, weekly, and monthly mining related production data.
Assist with the planning and design of blast holes, tie ups and charging plans as required and provide technical support to the Drill & Blast Team.
Assist with the planning and scheduling of drill and blast operations in line with the short term mine plan and integrate this work with other planning and operational areas.
With the support of the planning team, actively engage with the production team to communicate designs and plans to ensure that the drill & blast processes are optimised.
People accountabilities
Coordinate resources for the effective delivery of all production planning requirements
Coach, mentor and train the mine engineering team to ensure tasks are consistently completed to a high standard to ensure that mining operations can meet targets and operate efficiently and effectively.
Provide direction and leadership for mining engineers, graduate engineers and others

We need the right people. Our vision is to build a high performing mine technical services team to cover all technical mining engineering activities from short term to strategic mine planning, with all work completed on site and minimal reliance on external consultants.
We are looking for people who are highly motivated, have drive, energy and are genuinely passionate about the work they do and provide a positive impact.  Additionally, we are looking for people who see a challenge as an opportunity for personal growth and development and value working in a team towards a common goal.

Behaviour consistent with St Barbara Values
Ability to produce a PNG National Police Clearance (valid within the last 3 months) for site access purposes
Current unencumbered Papua New Guinea’s ‘C’ Class Driver’s Licence
A degree qualification in mining engineering or related discipline
High level of enthusiasm for the work with high performance goals for self and team
Effective multitasking skills and the ability to work under pressure
Excellent analytical and teamwork skills
Good written and verbal communication skills as well as good organizational and administrative skills.
Desirable
Experience as an OJT in Open Pit drill & blast and/or mine planning
