jobs.title: PNG Regional Fleet Coordinator
jobs.description:
Don’t come for an easy career. Stay for a rewarding one.
Santos is a global energy company committed to increasingly cleaner energy and fuels production, with operations across Australia, Papua New Guinea, Timor-Leste and North America.
We are currently PNG’s largest single investor and most active explorer, operating all the country’s producing oil fields and holding an extensive appraisal and exploration portfolio. Our aspirations and strategies reflect our genuine commitment to making a meaningful contribution to the lives of Papua New Guineans.
At Santos, our commitment is to be a global leader in the transition to cleaner energy and clean fuels, by helping the world decarbonise to reach net-zero emissions in an affordable and sustainable way.
Santos is one of Australia’s biggest domestic gas suppliers, a leading Asia Pacific LNG supplier and is committed to supplying the critical fuels such as oil and gas in a more sustainable way through decarbonising projects such as the Moomba CCS project.
For more than 65 years, Santos has been working in partnership with local communities, providing local jobs and business opportunities, safely and sustainably developing its natural gas resources, and powering industries and households.
What you’ll do:
Based in the Santos Port Moresby office, the Regional Fleet Coordinator will lead the coordination of fleet and workshop operations across the country. Your role will drive cost efficiency, safety, and operational reliability, ensuring all vehicle activities align with Santos’ Land Transport Procedure and PNG regulations.
Key Responsibilities:
Fleet Operations Management:
Lead all aspects of fleet operations, including pool vehicle oversight, workshop coordination, and cost allocation. Forecast operating costs, monitor vehicle utilisation, and ensure compliance with local transport laws, safety, mass and load limits.
Cost and Efficiency Initiatives:
Identify and deliver cost-saving measures, implement cost control systems, track compliance, and optimise asset utilisation to improve transparency and reduce financial leakage.
Team and Stakeholder Coordination:
Lead workshop maintenance teams and mechanics to minimise vehicle downtime and improve reliability. Act as the first point of contact for PNG-based staff, providing expert advice on fleet assets, land transport standards and best practice.
Training and awareness:
Develop and deliver targeted training programs on fleet operations and compliance, supporting the uplift of local capability and adherence to Santos standards.
Compliance and Technical Oversight:
Conduct regular fleet inspections, support incident investigations, and provide technical advice for decisions on vehicle grounding. Collaborate with internal teams to identify and address non-compliance, ensuring corrective actions are implemented effectively.
Governance and Safety:
Ensure full compliance with the Santos Management System (SMS), Delegation of Authority (DOA), and corporate governance and safety requirements.
What you’ll bring:
Your strong technical knowledge of mechanical systems for both light and heavy vehicles, with the capability to conduct mechanical inspections and prepare detailed reports following vehicle related incidents are key. Experience working with SAP and reporting tools will further support your success in this role along with:
Good working knowledge of Papua New Guinea (PNG) regulatory and vehicle registration requirements for light and heavy vehicles.
Practical experience in workshop parts management and supply chain processes.
Proven track record in vehicle workshop or fleet management operations.
Ability to deliver coordinated operational solutions across multiple remote locations.
Strong skills in process improvement, including process mapping, cost control, and data analytics.
Excellent communication and problem-solving skills to maintain smooth fleet operations.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel, for data analysis, reporting, and compliance tracking.
Trade qualification in Motor Mechanics or a related discipline would be highly regarded
What you’ll get:
Here, you’ll be amongst high-calibre people and get to work on industry-leading projects. We don’t shy away from solving tough problems at pace. We like it that way. You can expect to be challenged and supported; to learn and grow.
At Santos, we’re committed to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive. This means a place that is safe; where you are valued and respected, and your contribution is recognised and appreciated. Join us, and you’ll play a role in this too.
Each of our sites offer access to specific amenities that aim to create the best possible benefits to your health, wellbeing and performance.
What you’re part of:
Everywhere you turn you will be a part of a team who are coming together to contribute to our single uniting purpose - to provide reliable and affordable energy to help create a better world for everyone And because it’s not only what you do, but how you do it, you will also contribute to improving the living standards of the communities where we operate, building enduring and respectful relationships that serve a generation. It’s about each of us, and all of us – together.
How to Apply
Applications must be submitted via the online recruitment system before
COB 12 November 2025.
A requirement of this role is that you will need to have in place the legal work rights for PNG to apply.
Potential Scams
There are a number of fake adverts that are impersonating Santos Limited, in these instances you will receive an e-mail from a generic e-mail address. We do not make offers without interviews or due diligence taking place. You will know if an advert is genuine if you are directed to the Santos company careers page to apply which is
https://recruitment.santos.com/

Here you’ll make a difference
Save the Children is the world’s largest independent child rights development organization, making a difference to children’s lives in more than 100 countries. From emergency relief to long-term development, Save the Children secures a child’s right to health, education, and protection. At Save the Children, we attract bright and big-hearted people who are inspired to make a difference. Together, we are fearless in our pursuit of making lasting change for the children and communities who need it most. In Papua New Guinea, Save the Children currently implement programs in the sectors of health, education, child protection, child rights governance and livelihoods. The Child Nutrition and Social Protection Project is an 18-month project implemented from March 2025 to December 2026 in the provinces of East New Britain and Simbu.
Here your skills will be valued
Role Purpose
Reporting to the Deputy Team Leader – Operations, the Provincial Coordinator will lead the implementation of all activities in his/her assigned province. This role will focus on coordinating and overseeing all project activities at the provincial level, ensuring effective implementation, stakeholder engagement, and alignment with Save the Children and Government of PNG national objectives.
Key Areas of Accountability
Program Management and Delivery
Oversee the implementation of activities in the assigned province, including project participant registration, sensitization, and trainings.
Manage the recruitment, training, and supervision of Community Development Workers (CDW) in coordination with district teams and People & Culture.
Coordinate with District Officers and CDWs to ensure timely and quality implementation of project activities.
Monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) for activity delivery; address any bottlenecks at the provincial level. Develop/refine provincial implementation plans, ensuring alignment with national roll-out strategies.
Support the MEAL team in any post-distribution monitoring (PDM) activities in the province
Contribute to the analysis of project data and the development of recommendations for improving project performance at the provincial level
Ensure adherence to project timelines, budgets, and donor requirements for the province. Ensure timely and accurate reporting on project activities, including financial and narrative reports
Operational Management
Oversee the establishment and management of offices in the province. Manage day-to-day operations at the provincial level, including logistics, procurement, and administrative functions.
Coordinate with the Deputy Team Leader and national office to ensure alignment of operational processes and systems (e.g., supply chain, human resources, finance).
Ensure compliance with Save the Children's policies, procedures, and donor requirements.
Stakeholder Engagement and Coordination
Serve as the primary liaison with provincial government officials, Payment Service Providers (PSPs), and other key stakeholders to facilitate smooth project implementation.
Represent Save the Children in relevant coordination meetings and forums at the provincial level. Maintain strategic relationships with provincial-level stakeholders and partners.
Coordinate closely with government/counterpart provincial coordinators.
Capacity Building and Support
Identify capacity-building needs for provincial and district-level staff and coordinate training opportunities. Provide mentoring and support to District Officers and CDWs.
Facilitate knowledge sharing and best practices across districts within the province.
General
Comply with Save the Children policies and practice with respect to child safeguarding, code of conduct, health and safety, equal opportunities and other relevant policies and procedures.
Embody the Save the Children values in practice of Accountability, Ambition, Collaboration, Creativity, and Integrity. Work according to Save the Children’s mandate and child focus.
Work according to any other duties as assigned by the supervisor.
Child protection and safeguarding requirements
Maintain a child safe environment at the workplace and safeguard children’s rights, acting in the best interests of children at all times.
Maintain compliance with Save the Children’s
Child Safeguarding Policy
,
Code of Conduct
, and PSEAH policies and reporting processes among staff and volunteers.
Act as a role model by demonstrating highest standards of behavior towards children in private and professional life.
Never abuse the position of trust that comes with being a part of the Save the Children family.
Maintain a safe and positive relationship at all times when working with children and young people.
Respond to any concerns for the safety or wellbeing of a child in a program in accordance with internal reporting processes.
Health, safety, security and risk management
Be a role model for safety and security and comply with all workplace safety policy, procedure, work instructions and training.
Act safely at all times.
Report all incidents, injuries and potential hazards in a timely manner.
Participate in, and contribute to, health and safety awareness and improvements.
Be aware of, and consider, the risks associated with one’s daily work and apply appropriate mitigation measures in line with Save the Children’s policies and procedures.
All roles at Save the Children contribute to our impact for children.
At Save the Children, every role, whether in our programs or support services, plays a vital part in our impact for children. We are committed to creating a positive impact on the lives of children and their communities, and we value the contributions of every team member in achieving this vision.

Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field (e.g., Development Studies, Public Health, Social Sciences). Master’s degree is an advantage.
Minimum of five (5) years of experience in project management, preferably in social protection or nutrition programs.
Strong understanding of cash transfer programs and their implementation in developing contexts
Excellent leadership and team management skills.
Proven ability to work effectively with government stakeholders and diverse partners.
Proven ability to work effectively in complex, multi-stakeholder environments. Ability to think strategically, prioritize, problem-solve, and meet deadlines in a complex and challenging environment; must be culturally sensitive.
Excellent coordination and interpersonal skills with the ability to communicate and negotiate clearly and effectively at all levels and with a range of stakeholders (e.g., communities, government, donors). Proven external coordination and representation skills at a senior level.
Exhibit a strong work ethic with a high degree of flexibility with respect to working hours; ability to effectively plan and manage own time under pressure.
Excellent writing and verbal skills in English for reports and communications documents. Ability to present complex information in a succinct and compelling manner. Proficiency in Tok Pisin.
Familiarity with the local context and culture of the assigned province.
Additional Information

jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
As an Advisor Contracts, you will play a key role in ensuring Newmont’s regional contracts for our Papua New Guinea operations are effectively managed, compliant, and aligned with our global procurement strategies. Your expertise will help secure critical goods and services, mitigate risks, and strengthen supplier and stakeholder relationships, all while supporting our commitment to safe, sustainable, and responsible mining.
As part of our team, you will
Deliver the procurement plan to schedule, ensuring projects stay on track and within budget.
Work closely with site stakeholders to coordinate activities, mitigate scope creep, and maintain alignment with organizational objectives.
Administer the full lifecycle of contracts, assisting the Team Lead - Category Management in implementing category strategies and ensuring appropriate contracts are in place for sourcing materials and services.
Collaborate with site operational teams to ensure contracts meet strategic objectives and support operational success.
Implement Newmont’s strategic sourcing strategies for goods and services in line with the Strategic Sourcing Playbook.
Maintain strong working relationships with internal partners and key clients, providing visibility of the supply chain vision and ensuring internal stakeholder satisfaction.
Build and sustain strong supplier relationships, ensuring open communication, timely resolution of contract-related issues, and favourable negotiation of contract changes.
Supervise all contracts and procurement activities within the sub-category to ensure compliance with legal, regulatory, and company policies, including health, safety, and environmental standards.
Assess and manage risks associated with contracts, including potential legal liabilities and performance issues.
Provide regular updates on contract status, performance, and compliance, contributing insights to support the development of regional procurement methodologies.
Prerequisites for your success in this role
Tertiary qualification in a relevant field, such as engineering, law, business, finance, or supply chain.
Proven experience in contract management, procurement, or sourcing in mining, oil & gas, energy, or engineering industries.
Experience in end-to-end sourcing activities and contract management for direct and indirect services is essential.
Practical exposure to mining operations in PNG, including familiarity with regulatory requirements for import/export, mobilisation, and the handling of goods.
Strong knowledge of legal principles, compliance requirements, and procurement best practices.
Proficiency in SAP, Ariba, or similar ERP/eProcurement systems.
Skilled in negotiations, supplier management, and contract performance evaluation.
Strong technical skills in strategic sourcing, supplier relationship management, contracts administration, negotiations, risk identification, and dispute resolution.
Demonstrated ability to analyse data, monitor KPIs, conduct audits or reviews, and make data-driven decisions while maintaining accuracy and compliance across multiple contracts.
Excellent interpersonal, stakeholder engagement, and communication skills, with the ability to influence, collaborate, and foster strong relationships internally and externally.
Your work environment
Our Brisbane-based team enjoy flexible Monday to Friday work options to balance working from home and in the office. Our modern Fortitude Valley office is conveniently located near public transport and local cafés. Occasional travel to site operations and other interstate Newmont hubs may be required to support the broader team.
This is an exciting opportunity to contribute within Newmont’s Sustainability and Development function, supporting contract management activities that directly impact operational success. You’ll collaborate with diverse teams and external partners while working in a dynamic, fast-paced environment where safety, compliance, and sustainable practices are core values.
Why Join Newmont
At Newmont, you’ll be part of the world’s leading gold company, dedicated to creating value and improving lives through responsible mining. We offer:
A global network of operations and career growth opportunities.
A values-driven culture that prioritises safety, inclusion, and sustainability.
Competitive compensation, benefits, and professional development programs.
The chance to make a meaningful impact on both local communities and global industry standards.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!

Santos is a global energy company committed to increasingly cleaner energy and fuels production, with operations across Australia, Papua New Guinea, Timor-Leste and North America.

Our aspirations and strategies reflect our genuine commitment to making a meaningful contribution to the lives of Papua New Guineans.
At Santos, our commitment is to be a global leader in the transition to cleaner energy and clean fuels, by helping the world decarbonise to reach net-zero emissions in an affordable and sustainable way.
Santos is one of Australia’s biggest domestic gas supplier, a leading Asia Pacific LNG supplier and is committed to supplying the critical fuels such as oil and gas in a more sustainable way through decarbonising projects such as the Moomba CCS project.
For more than 65 years, Santos has been working in partnership with local communities, providing local jobs and business opportunities, safely and sustainably developing its natural gas resources, and powering industries and households.
What you’ll do:
Santos Foundation is seeking a dedicated and detail-oriented

Ensure transparency and maintain a clear audit trail for all contract activities.

Each of our sites offer access to specific amenities that aim to create the best possible benefits to your health, wellbeing and performance.
What you’re part of:
Everywhere you turn you will be a part of a team who are coming together to contribute to our single uniting purpose - to provide reliable and affordable energy to help create a better world for everyone And because it’s not only what you do, but how you do it, you will also contribute to improving the living standards of the communities where we operate, building enduring and respectful relationships that serve a generation. jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
As a Technician, Processing, you’ll play a key role in operating critical sections of the process plant, including grinding circuits, flotation, and thickener operations. Your work ensures safety, efficiency, and production targets are met shift by shift, contributing directly to Newmont’s operational success.
As Part of Our Team, You Will
Prioritize Safety
: Ensure compliance with all HSE policies, report hazards, and actively monitor plant conditions.
Collaborate Effectively
: Work constructively with diverse teams and participate in shift handovers, toolbox meetings, and training.
Drive Production
: Operate plant equipment, complete inspections, and maintain housekeeping standards.
Control Costs
: Identify and report cost-saving opportunities and minimize waste.
Prerequisites for Your Success in This Role
Proven experience in heavy industry, preferably mining (essential).
Grade 10 education minimum.
Tertiary qualifications and metalliferous processing certificates are highly regarded.
Class 6 PNG Driver’s License.
Strong communication, attention to detail, time management, and technical knowledge in mineral processing.
Safety-conscious, proactive problem solver, team player, and adaptable to changing work conditions.
Your Work Environment
28:14 FIFO roster with flexibility for extended hours and higher duties.
Fast-paced, safety-focused mining operation on Lihir Island.
Collaborative and diverse team culture.
Why Join Newmont
Be part of a global leader in mining committed to safety, sustainability, and innovation.
Grow your career through training and development opportunities.
Work in a supportive environment that values your contribution and well-being.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply before the closing date: 10 November 2025 – we’d love to hear from you!

About us
K92 Mining Limited operates the Kainantu Gold Mine in the Eastern Highlands Province. Since we launched in 2016, we've grown gold production every year, boosting Papua New Guinea's economy. We take pride in supporting your communities, with nearly 94% of our team members being fellow PNG locals.
Looking ahead, we will significantly increase our gold production in the next three years. This expansion means that K92 is a place for building a stable career, contributing to the community, and being a key part of our success.
About the role
This role will be responsible for controlling, monitoring and maintaining the machines and equipment used to crush, transfer and pump ore, water, and reagents to get high quality gold concentrates for K92 mining company.
Another function of this role is setting the controls and observing gauges and other instrumentation to monitor progress and check for malfunctions, leaks, and other faults

Key accountabilities of this position include.
Operators are also responsible for overseeing work is being done in a safe manner and to K92 safety regulations and standard.

Collect 2hrs samples.
Liaise with maintenance personal working in the area of responsibility.
Assist in isolation and de-isolation of equipment.
Preparing and measuring the reagents (PAX, CMC, Hydrated lime, and Flocculation) that are used in the processing plant.
About You
To be considered for this role, you will have some or all the following.
Minimum of Grade 10
An appropriate trades trade certificate
Minimum of (5) years’ experience working in the l Processing Plant in a supervisory role.
To be physically fit
To enjoy practical and manual activities
To be able to read and follow written instructions.
The ability to work as part of a team.
Good hand-eye co-ordination
Good problem-solving and analytical skills
Life at K92
Our core values — Collaboration, Accountability, Respect, Excellence, and Safety — are central to our operations and fundamental to our success. K92 upholds a commitment to equal opportunity, striving to ensure that every individual can reach their highest potential without experiencing discrimination.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
We believe in sharing our success with our employees. In addition to competitive salaries, we offer participation in long- and short-term incentive plans. We also offer savings programs, medical assistance, as well as access to our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
If you share our values and are looking for your next career step, come join us on this exciting journey. Submit your application through our website today.

jobs.description:
KutMor Limited is a nationally owned landowner company that services the Oil & Gas Industry in the Kutubu and Moran areas in the Southern Highlands Province of Papua New Guinea.
We are seeking a highly motivated and experienced candidate for the following role within our Facility Maintenance Department. This is a 4/4 FIFO role located in Kutubu, SHP and reports to the Facility Maintenance Coordinator.
Facility Maintenance Supervisor
Job Summary
The Facility Maintenance Supervisor is responsible for overseeing the day-to-day maintenance operations of camp infrastructure, including accommodation, utilities, buildings, and associated services. This role ensures that all maintenance activities are carried out safely, efficiently, and in compliance with company standards and client expectations. The Supervisor leads a team of tradespeople and contractors, coordinates work schedules, and ensures timely completion of maintenance tasks to support uninterrupted camp operations.
Key Responsibility Areas
Lead and supervise maintenance teams responsible for camp infrastructure, including buildings, plumbing, electrical systems, HVAC, and grounds.

Trade qualification in a relevant field (e.g., electrical, plumbing, refrigeration)

Knowledge of maintenance planning and scheduling systems
Familiarity with safety and compliance requirements in remote camp environments
Good communication and interpersonal skills
Proficient in computer-based applications, including Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.

jobs.title: Digital Transformation, EdTech & eLearning Roles, PNG
jobs.industry: Education and Training, IT, Non Government Organisations (NGOs)
jobs.description:
Shape the Future of Education in PNG
Do you want to help build inclusive, future-ready education and training systems in Papua New Guinea (PNG)?
Are you excited by the role digital tools and innovation can play in system-wide transformation?
Catalpa is growing a pool of outstanding education and digital leaders for upcoming opportunities — and we’d love to hear from you!
Flexible opportunities: full-time, part-time, short-term, or longer-term
About Us
At Catalpa, we’re all about creating real impact. We’re a global development organisation that believes bright ideas—mixed with technology, creativity, and local know-how—can solve tough challenges.
Our team is a mix of engineers, designers, educators, and project delivery folk. Together, we work on projects that matter and actually change lives. One of the things we’re most proud of?  Making learning accessible and engaging for communities that are often left out.  Our work is meaningful, innovative, and, honestly, pretty cool. Check us out at
www.catalpa.io
.
About the Opportunities
We are picking up the pace with preparing for new projects in PNG and want to connect with professionals passionate about digital transformation, eLearning, education technology and innovation, and education system strengthening. As Catalpa continues to grow, so does our appetite for awesome talent!
In these senior roles, you’ll:
Partner with government, training providers, and institutions to design and implement digital systems that strengthen governance, planning, and evidence-based decision-making.
Drive an innovation agenda by piloting digital tools, eLearning platforms, and online training solutions that improve student engagement, graduate employability, and system resilience.
Ensure digital solutions are policy-aligned, user-centred, and sustainable — designed for lasting impact.
Your work will be both visionary and practical: grounded in evidence, shaped by users, and responsive to PNG’s unique context.
This is what we’re looking for - we’d love to meet people who have experience and expertise in any of the following areas:
Leading the co-design and rollout of educational data systems, digital platforms, or performance tools.
Designing and implementing innovative elearning approaches (e.g., micro-learning management systems, mobile tools, e-assessments, etc) with a focus on usability and sustainability.
Developing demand-driven digital pilots such as:
Behaviour change campaigns to improve enrolment or re-engage learners.
Job-matching and graduate–employer connection platforms.
Innovations in green/blue economy training, digital career counselling, or wraparound services.
Developing digital curricula, online training modules, and blended learning approaches tailored to PNG’s diverse contexts.
Utilising instructional design and digital pedagogy principles to develop relevant learning content. Bonus points if you have experience supporting teacher training and adult learning.
About You:
You’ll have a strong track record in digital transformation, education technology, eLearning or innovation leadership.
Skilled in co-design, stakeholder engagement, and adapting solutions to local contexts (e.g., low-resource or culturally diverse settings).
A systems thinker who is practical, collaborative, and outcomes-focused.
Note, these roles are open to Papua New Guinean applicants only
Extra awesome if you bring:
Familiarity with DFAT-funded programs, working confidently with government, donors, and institutions
Knowledge of accessibility standards and inclusive education practices.
Commitment to building PNG-led digital leadership capacity
Sound like your kind of challenge? Great—let’s talk!
At Catalpa, we design better futures. We're a mission-driven organisation combining technology, design thinking, and deep contextual knowledge to build practical solutions to complex challenges. Our work spans education, health, governance, and livelihoods — and we’re proud to keep people at the centre of everything we do.
Joining Catalpa means:
Being part of nationwide education and workforce reforms in PNG
Piloting creative digital solutions with potential for national scale
Working with a collaborative, human-first team that values learning and local leadership
Doing meaningful work that has real impact on people’s lives
Work environment
We work in a creative, supportive environment with colleagues who come from diverse walks of life, and we value the perspectives they bring. We pay attention to the details, and we work together to achieve the best we can. Importantly, we work here because we love what we do and the impact we can have.
We know people’s lives include many obligations outside of work, so we aim to create a flexible work environment that includes remote work options, generous family leave, and return-to-work policies to support new parents. We know we do our best work when we take care of ourselves and communities. We take two weeks off at the end of each year to recharge and refresh.
Fit
Catalpa staff believe in the potential of technology to transform lives for the better. Our team members are flexible and can handle working across a broad range of responsibilities. They don’t mind rolling up their sleeves to solve thorny challenges that take time, patience, and creativity. We are friendly and care about the people with whom we work, always seeking to build and nurture relationships for the long-term.
Catalpa seeks to provide a fair and equal employment opportunity for all people, regardless of race, color, religious creed, national origin, ancestry, age, gender, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, or marital status. We especially welcome applications from people with diverse backgrounds.
Catalpa prioritises the safeguarding of all people, including the prevention of sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment and the safeguarding of children. Engagement of personnel within Catalpa is conditional upon the outcome of background checks, and there is a requirement for all candidates to disclose any current charges or previous convictions regarding assault, abuse or exploitation of children or adults, as well as regarding fraud and/or corruption.  All Catalpa personnel are required to abide by Catalpa’s Child Safeguarding Policy, Prevention of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment Policy and
Code of Conduct.
How to apply
Apply now with your up-to-date resume and a short cover letter telling us why you’d be a great fit for this role. Head to
catalpa.io/work-with-us
to submit your application.
Got questions? Email
[email protected]
with Digital Transformation - Education roles in the subject line (but please send your CV via the website, not email).
Expressions of interest close on
7 November 2025
.
We can’t wait to hear from you!

Nature of the consultancy:
The consultancy involves providing technical expertise and coordination support to assess, strengthen, and implement multi-hazard early warning systems in Papua New Guinea, in alignment with the global Early Warnings for All (EW4ALL) initiative and national disaster risk reduction priorities.
Project Context and Scope:
The International Organization for Migration (IOM), in collaboration with national governments and regional partners, is implementing a project to strengthen multi-hazard Early Warning Systems (EWS) in Fiji, Papua New Guinea (PNG), and Vanuatu. The initiative supports the global Early Warnings for All (EW4ALL) initiative and aims to enhance disaster preparedness and resilience including through inclusive, community-based approaches. In Papua New Guinea, the consultant will lead technical assessments, stakeholder engagement, and knowledge exchange activities to improve the effectiveness of EWS and contribute to regional learning session. To provide technical expertise and coordination support for the assessment, enhancement, and implementation of multi-hazard early warning systems in Papua New Guinea, aligned with EW4ALL pillars and regional disaster risk reduction priorities.
Organizational Department / Unit to which the Consultant is contributing:
Emergency and Disaster Management Unit
Responsibilities
Category A Consultants: Tasks to be performed under this contract
:
The consultant will:
Conduct a comprehensive desktop review of existing EWS in PNG, assessing progress against the four EW4ALL pillars:
Risk Knowledge
Monitoring & Forecasting
Warning Dissemination
Preparedness & Response
Identify and map key stakeholders, systems, gaps, and priority areas for improvement.
Validate findings through consultations with national and local stakeholders; update the EWS Review Report accordingly.
Develop a EWS Situation Brief and Gap Analysis Report.
Lead the design, planning, and coordination of the National Early Warning Systems (EWS) Workshop in Papua New Guinea, including development of the agenda, identification of key stakeholders and speakers, logistical arrangements, and facilitation support. Ensure alignment with national disaster risk reduction priorities and the EW4ALL framework.
Produce a comprehensive workshop report, capturing key discussions, recommendations, commitments, and lessons learned. Coordinate follow-up actions with participating agencies, including government counterparts, development partners, and community representatives to ensure continuity and implementation of agreed outcomes.
Conduct stakeholder mapping of private sector actors and telecommunications companies to identify potential partners for advancing EWS implementation, including assessing existing capabilities, technologies, and service coverage, and designing targeted engagement strategies and collaborative actions.
Work closely with relevant government authorities to ensure alignment with national policies and regulatory frameworks, and ensure coordination with the relevant government entities, UN agencies, development partners and key stakeholders.
Support the design and coordination of a regional peer-to-peer learning exchange workshop including providing inputs to the workshop materials and coordinate with participants and facilitators.
Assist in implementing Community-Based Disaster Risk Management (CBDRM) and EWS interventions in target communities, including support installation of operational EWS, and facilitate tabletop and simulation exercises. Deploy surveys to assess EWS usage and access among communities.
Collaborate with IOM country, regional, and HQ teams to develop concept notes and funding proposals.
Contribute to donor reporting, briefing materials, and visibility products.
Perform other duties as assigned.
Key Deliverables
EWS Review Report (draft and final)
EWS Situation Brief and Gap Analysis Report
Workshop concept note and final report
Community-level EWS implementation support documentation
Survey results and analysis
Contributions to donor reports and proposals, and relevant visibility products
Performance indicators for the evaluation of results
Timely submission of high-quality deliverables and reports.
Effective coordination with government and key stakeholders.
Successful organization and facilitation of workshops and consultations.
Completion of stakeholder mapping and community-level activities.
Quality technical inputs provided to support project implementation and reporting.
Qualifications
Education and Experience
Master’s Degree in Geography, Environmental Sciences, Disaster Management, International Relations, Environmental Engineering, or related field.
Alternatively, a Bachelor’s Degree in the above fields with at least 10 years of relevant experience.
Minimum 8 years (Master’s) or 10–15 years (Bachelor’s) of professional experience in disaster risk management, early warning systems, or related fields.
Proven experience in project management, stakeholder engagement, and workshop facilitation.

jobs.title: E & I Technician
jobs.description:
Don’t come for an easy career. Stay for a rewarding one.
Santos is a global energy company committed to increasingly cleaner energy and fuels production, with operations across Australia, Papua New Guinea, Timor-Leste and North America.
We are currently PNG’s largest single investor and most active explorer, operating all the country’s producing oil fields and holding an extensive appraisal and exploration portfolio. Our aspirations and strategies reflect our genuine commitment to making a meaningful contribution to the lives of Papua New Guineans.
At Santos, our commitment is to be a global leader in the transition to cleaner energy and clean fuels, by helping the world decarbonise to reach net-zero emissions in an affordable and sustainable way.
Santos is one of Australia’s biggest domestic gas suppliers, a leading Asia Pacific LNG supplier and is committed to supplying the critical fuels such as oil and gas in a more sustainable way through decarbonising projects such as the Moomba CCS project.
For more than 65 years, Santos has been working in partnership with local communities, providing local jobs and business opportunities, safely and sustainably developing its natural gas resources, and powering industries and households.
What you’ll do:
Based in Gobe, PNG, the E&I Technician maintains and troubleshoots Process Control Instrumentation across Well Heads, Processing Plants, remote communication sites, Valve Stations, and the Kumul Marine Terminal.
You’ll work closely with Production and engineering teams to support daily production targets and provide technical support to contractors on operational and HSES matters.
This is a 28:28 FIFO role.
Key Responsibilities
Troubleshoot and repair breakdowns on all instruments and electrical equipment using proven techniques to identify and fix faults.
Provide training and mentorship to junior local instrument technicians to build their skills and ensure successful task completion.
Inspect, troubleshoot, and repair gas-fired equipment across the project.
Install, troubleshoot, and repair various oil and gas meters, including hardware repairs, meter configuration, calibration, and security.
Verify and monitor programmable logic controllers (PLCs), adjust programs, troubleshoot event sequences, and reprogram as needed.
Assist the instrumentation system administrator with programming, maintenance, and repairs of the distributed control system.
Plan and conduct preventative maintenance inspections on all instrumentation equipment, coordinating schedules and documenting findings.
Troubleshoot and maintain ESD, smoke, thermal, and gas detection systems, performing functional tests and fault isolation.
Install new instrumentation equipment, including detailed layouts, point-to-point drawings, material procurement, installation, and commissioning.
Ensure compliance with Santos Management System (SMS), Delegation of Authority (DOA), and Corporate Governance and Safety standards.
What you’ll bring:
Proven experience as an Instrument Technician in a similar industry, demonstrating practical skills and knowledge relevant to the role.
Practical knowledge of basic instrumentation and process control.
Experience working in Oil & Gas or Mining industries, familiar with plant processes and equipment.
Competent in repair, installation, and calibration of Process Control Instrumentation.
Ability to read, understand and interpret basic Instrument/Electrical and pneumatic loop drawings.
Familiarity with Distributed Control Systems (DCS).
Ideally, you’ll hold an Electronics or Instrumentation Trade Certificate or be a Licensed Electrician cross-trained as an Instrument Technician with relevant certification.
What you’ll get:
Here, you’ll be amongst high-calibre people and get to work on industry-leading projects. We don’t shy away from solving tough problems at pace. We like it that way. You can expect to be challenged and supported; to learn and grow.
At Santos, we’re committed to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive. This means a place that is safe; where you are valued and respected, and your contribution is recognised and appreciated. Join us, and you’ll play a role in this too.

JOB VACANCY ANNOUNCEMENT
POSITION TITLE:
DRIVER
MSF BACKGROUND
Médecins Sans Frontières (Doctors Without Borders)
is a private, non-profit international humanitarian organization founded in 1971 and operating in 70 countries worldwide. MSF delivers medical assistance to people affected by armed conflict, epidemics, natural disasters, and exclusion from health care. MSF aids people based on need, irrespective of race, religion, gender, or political affiliation.
PROJECT CONTEXT
In PNG, MSF has been working since 2007 in Lae, Tari, Bougainville, Gulf Province, and NCD Province. In 2024, MSF started a new project in Jiwaka province to enhance access to care for survivors of violence in Jiwaka province and is now working to support the Department of Health to improve access to care for patients in JIWAKA and the Highlands.
General Role
Performing the tasks of transporting authorized goods and passengers in an MSF vehicle, ensuring its technical and safety conditions, and respecting the country's traffic rules and MSF security rules, to provide a safe, smooth and efficient service.
Main Accountability
Checking daily, the technical conditions of the assigned vehicle (state of the tires, oil, fuel, brakes, radio equipment, spare parts, etc.), performing weekly checks according to the MSF Logbook, refilling it when necessary, and keeping it clean to ensure it can be driven in perfect condition. Carrying out a handover if another user uses the vehicle
Ensuring the security of passengers in the vehicle, driving carefully, observing speed limits and traffic rules in the country, as well as MSF security rules, to avoid car accidents.
Ensuring all passengers have all necessary papers in order before travelling, and ensuring non-MSF staff sign disclaimers of responsibility before using the vehicle
Ensuring correct loading and unloading of the vehicle, submitting the documents to the receiver of the goods, checking the status of delivered goods, returning the duly completed documents to Logistics, and ensuring that the goods have the necessary documents
Ensuring that all vehicle documents and the driver's driving license are valid and in the vehicle.
Informing the line manager of any incident involving the transportation of passengers and/or goods.
Knowing how to use all types of radios, codes, call numbers, and radio alphabets by heart and communicating with base according to MSF communications policy to inform the driver's position and any potential implications.
Knowing and respecting the security rules related to vehicle movements, specifically those related to customs, checkpoints, and roadblocks. Ensuring all passengers know and respect the security rules
Specific Responsibilities
VEHICLE CHECKS/MAINTENANCE
Ensure that hand over is done at the beginning and end of each shift. Report to your line manager and record any incident in the vehicle handover log book.
Carry-out vehicle tools, fire-extinguisher and first aid, inventory during handover
Ensure that vehicles are kept clean at all time (before and after use)
Ensure that movements are recorded in the movement log book.
Ensure that Vehicle refuel is done regularly as per schedule.
Ensure that the vehicle is always in good condition by daily checks of the technical conditions of the assigned vehicle, perform weekly check according to the MSF Logbook, refilling it when necessary, and keeping it clean to ensure it can be driven in perfect conditions.
TRANSPORTATION OF MATERIALS
Be flexible and help with loading and offloading vehicle or carrying anything for the log team
Ensure correct loading and unloading of the vehicle, in particular:
SAFETY & SECURITY
Ensure the security of passengers in the vehicle, driving carefully, observing speed limits and traffic rules in the country as well as MSF driving policy and security rules in order to avoid car accidents.
Ensure that vehicles seat belts are functional and visible for passengers to use.
Ensure that passengers fasten their seat belt before departure. NO SEAT BELT NO DEPARTURE
Ensure all passengers have all necessary papers in order before travelling, and ensuring non MSF staff sign disclaimers of responsibility before using the vehicle.
Inform the line manager of any incident involving the transportation of passengers or goods.
Know how to use all types of radios, codes, call numbers and radio alphabets by heart and communicate with base according to MSF communications policy to inform the driver's position and any potential implications.

coordination of our fieldwork teams of interviewers, including running project briefings, conducting field visits, monitoring team progress, and planning logistics
providing accurate and timely reporting on fieldwork status to the field management team
following our fieldwork compliance requirements for ISO using our existing procedures
regular travel domestically in PNG to conduct small team briefings and check on team progress
checking questionnaire scripts that are programmed onto tablet devices by our data team to see that they work correctly before running briefings with the fieldwork team
supporting the PNG General Manager as required
The role suits a person with flexibility in working hours, including work into early evenings and on weekends as necessary.
You will report to the PNG General Manager with line reporting to the Regional Operations Manager.
The Person
You must have a university degree in any field including business, with a good academic record.
You will ideally have up to 2 years of commercial work experience in any field, but newer graduates are also welcome to apply. An understanding of any of the following fields would be an advantage but not essential: market research, operations, information technology, project management, or human resources.
The role will suit you if you are interested in human behaviour, in learning to lead small teams of people, and logistics. You will have the following qualities:
a genuine interest in people’s views and opinions
the confidence to learn to lead teams
good communication skills and the ability to communicate with people from all walks of life
the highest level of personal integrity and honesty
a team player attitude and like working collaboratively
a quality focus
a high standard of written and spoken English
Details
Salary and benefits are commensurate with skills and experience.

jobs.title: Project Officer
jobs.description:
With more than 40 years of experience working in PNG, World Vision Papua New Guinea (WVPNG) focuses on helping the most vulnerable children and adults experience the fullness of life.  Inspired by our Christian faith, WVPNG has an exciting opportunity for someone who may be looking for a change and wants to become part of a dynamic team.
We are currently looking for a suitable, qualified, experienced, and highly motivated professional to fill the
Project Officer - CIRCAR
to be based in
Morobe Province
,
Papua New Guinea.
PURPOSE OF THE POSITION
The Project Officer – CIRCAR supports and coordinates implementation of nature-based solution activities under the Live and Learn–CIRCAR project. The role ensures that nature-based solution activities are effectively implemented with the grey solutions implemented by the ARUP, TSSP and Department of Works and Highways across project communities along the Markham highway in Lae, Morobe Province and particularly children and youth, are empowered to participate in consultation regarding which nature-based solution is practical. Under the supervision of the Area Program Manager, the Project Officer will provide effective and efficient support in planning, implementation, coordination, and management of the project.
MAJOR ROLES & RESPONSIBILITIES
Project Implementation
Lead and support project implementation, and coordination, engagement with project participants and stakeholders, engage with Live and Learn in the planning of activities against the workplan and lead community engagements and capacity building initiatives.
Technical Support and capacity building
Provide training and mentoring to local partners, Village Health Assistants (VHAs), schools, and youth groups on climate adaptation, preparedness, and environmental stewardship and nature-based solutions.
Budget Management
Support the finance and admin team relating to project implementation, including preparation of cash requests and acquittals, ensure timely management and resource utilization in line with the developed Annual and Quarterly work plans and support the coordination and logistics for workshops and field visits
Monitoring, reporting & Learning
Collect and analyse data on NbS activities and indicators. Support participatory monitoring and documentation of lessons learned, case studies, and success stories for donor reporting
Community and Stakeholder Engagement
Strengthen coordination with partners and government. Facilitate community dialogues and youth participation in local NbS initiatives.
EDUCATIONAL QUALIFICATION/SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE & EXPERIENCE
Minimum 2–3 years’ experience in community development, climate change, or DRR programming.
Experience working with government agencies or international NGOs preferred.
Experience in engaging with partners and other stakeholders.
Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage personal workload and meet deadlines
Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Climate Change, Development Studies, or related field.
Certification in Disaster Risk Reduction, Climate Adaptation, or Environmental Management is an asset
The position requires traveling to the Area program
Be available to work weekends and on short notice.
Physically fit with no underlying medical conditions.
Good communication skills in written and spoken English
Interested applicants should submit the following documents all in one PDF file before;
6 October 2025, 12:00 AM UTC
Expression of interest
Detailed CV
Valid Police & Medical Clearance Certificate
World Vision is committed to the principles of workplace diversity. Qualified women and people with disabilities are encouraged to apply.
World Vision is committed to the protection of children. We do not employ staff whose background is not aligned with our child protection practices. Hence employment is conditional upon successful completion of all applicable background checks, including criminal record checks, where possible.
We appreciate the time it takes to prepare your application. Please note that only short-listed candidates suitable for interviews will be contacted. If you do not hear from World Vision within
two (2) weeks
of the closing date, please consider your application unsuccessful.

Applications are invited from suitably qualified candidates for the following position within the University:
Administration Officer (Overseas Recruitment)
About the Role
The Papua New Guinea University of Technology is seeking a capable and detail-oriented Recruitment Admin Officer to join its Human Resources Division. This role plays a key part in supporting recruitment operations across the main campus and affiliate colleges, including SUSU Campus. The successful candidate will be responsible for managing recruitment documentation, coordinating logistics, and ensuring compliance with best practices in hiring.
Duties & Responsibilities
Provide mentoring and leadership to the Junior team members.
Provide recruitment report updates to senior managers as and when requested.
Assist payroll team with payroll-appointment cases to resolve the case.
Provide recruitment data to senior managers for budget purposes.
Provide assistance to the housing officer when and if need be.
Collaborate with printery team regarding recruitment printing requests.
Collaborate with all departments/schools regarding their recruitment requests and/or appointment requests.
Administer the end-to-end recruitment processes including advertising, shortlisting, interview coordination, onboarding, final documentation for data entry, and data entry into the Chris HR-Payroll system.
Process and issue appointment letters and employment contracts for citizen and non-citizen staff for both academic and non-academic positions.
Administer all new entry visa applications for non-citizen staff and their dependents.

Provide assistance to staff office with the non-citizen’s visa extension application from document compilation to the actual lodgments in collaboration with the PNG Immigration Office in Lae Branch as well as the Head Office in Port Moresby.

jobs.description:
Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
Joining our Commercial team, you will support the Materials Team Lead with all K92 Mining import/export cargo movements to site, whilst assisting in facilitating payments to freight companies by correctly processing all necessary documentation. You will work to minimize the impact of the section on the environment and ensure the workplace health & safety of employees, contractors and other stakeholders are maintained.
Key Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position mean you will
Ensure the prompt delivery arrangements for all import / export freight as required
Achieve weekly and daily priorities, and report on activity and outcomes
Ensure that all aspects of Material movements are undertaken in accordance with established policy and procedures. Ensuring that safety is paramount to all tasks performed.
Assist the Logistics Team Lead to Investigate discrepancies and incidents.
Ensure the timely completion of all tasks
Register completion of materials to Kumian Site and Port warehouse ensuring conformation that deliveries are completed to the K92 Mine schedules and plans.
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential that you have the following
Understanding of Pronto to support logistics requirements
Experience with storage and handling of Dangerous goods
Experience in Microsoft suite office tools – Excel, Word
Class 6 License minimum
RII or Proven VOC for forklift operations
High problem-solving capability
Excellent written and verbal communication skills
Ability to communicate clearly with people at all levels of the organisation and engage all relevant stakeholders
Minimum 3-5 years’ experience in logistics industry with relevant experience within material shipping and logistics
Minimum 3-5yrs driving and operating experience
Mining Industry experience preferred.
Life at K92
K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.
In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
THIS POSITION IS OPEN ONLY TO CANDIDATES WHO HAVE THE RIGHT TO LIVE & WORK IN PNG WITHOUT SPONSORSHIP
